title: Play rules
summary: A play rule limits when a track may play and how often it may repeat. You create named rules here and apply them to tracks or to whole playlists. Separation is a play rule too.

entities.text: From and to, in station time, with optional weekdays. A window may cross midnight, for example 22:00 to 02:00.
The track does not start again until this long after its last start, for example 72 hours.
No track of the same artist starts until this long after the artist's last start, whichever playlist the other track came from, for example 2 hours.

The most times the track may start within the same clock hour. The limit applies to each track separately, also when the rule is set on a playlist. To change how often a playlist plays in a clock, set an override of the playlist's placement in that clock (for example, Spread with a count).
The tracks and playlists the rule applies to. A playlist rule is checked for each of its tracks separately.

entities.term: A play rule limits, a placement rule demands
entities.text: A play rule never puts a track on air. How often a playlist appears in the hour, for example two jingles, is the playlist's placement rule; the play rule decides which track is allowed in that slot.

usage: A rule can combine a time window, a track interval, an artist interval, and a per-hour limit; at least one must be set, and all set parts must pass. Intervals are entered as hours and minutes and cannot be longer than the play log is kept (Settings, Retention). A track follows its own rules and the rules of its playlists. Only aired and planned items count; missed items do not.
steps: Click Add rule and enter a name that says what it does.
Set a time window, a track or artist interval, a per-hour limit, or a combination.
Save, then choose the tracks and playlists the rule applies to.
Save the clocks that use these playlists and read their warnings for hours in which no track passes.
mistakes: Setting only one end of the time window. Set both times or neither.
Expecting a rule to make a track play more often. Rules only block; placement rules create the slots.
Restricting every jingle of a playlist to the same window. Outside it, the jingle slots are skipped and you get warnings.
An interval longer than the play log retention. It is refused, because the history it needs is deleted; keep the play log longer or shorten the interval.
A fill playlist with no track interval. Its tracks may repeat within the hour, and the clock save warns about it.

example.title: Music rotation and jingles
example.text: "Music rotation": track interval 72 h, artist interval 2 h, applied to the music playlists; a song plays at most once in three days, and two songs of one artist are at least two hours apart. "Jingles": track interval 20 min, at most 2 per hour, applied to the jingle playlist; with the placement rule Spread 2, the jingles may repeat within a day but never twice in 20 minutes.

operations.create: At least one limit is required.
operations.edit: Changes apply to hours planned from now on.
operations.delete: A rule applied to any track or playlist cannot be deleted. The message lists them; remove the rule from them first.

name.label: Name
name.text: Say what the rule does, for example "Music rotation" or "Morning 06:00 to 10:00".

window_from.label: From
window_from.text: Start of the allowed time, HH:MM in station time. Set together with To.

window_to.label: To
window_to.text: End of the allowed time. Earlier than From when the window crosses midnight.

weekdays.label: Weekdays
weekdays.text: Days on which the window applies. None chosen means every day. For a window across midnight, the day it starts.

min_interval_minutes.label: Track interval
min_interval_minutes.text: Hours and minutes between two starts of the same track, for example 72 h. At most the play log retention.

artist_min_interval_minutes.label: Artist interval
artist_min_interval_minutes.text: Hours and minutes between two starts of tracks of the same artist, for example 2 h. At most the play log retention.

max_per_hour.label: Plays track per hour
max_per_hour.text: The most starts of the same track within one clock hour. It applies to each track of the playlist separately. To change how often a playlist plays in a clock, override its placement rule in that clock (for example, Spread with a count).

notes.label: Notes
notes.text: Why the rule exists, for your own reference.

track_ids.label: Tracks
track_ids.text: Tracks the rule applies to directly.

playlist_ids.label: Playlists
playlist_ids.text: Playlists whose every track follows the rule.
